requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.
verdict_reason: verified high finding(s) backed by receipts: requirement-tests-1, logic-edge-1

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 170/170 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The attribute is not emitted for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets. A context-free reviewer might call this a gap against 'all generated code', but ledger L7 records no preference there and says to follow the requirement. The change also documents the limitation in the README.
product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: Types with SuppressSourceGeneration=true get no formatter and so no attribute. This is deliberate and the README and a test both state it.
Receipts/Req2297ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/2), passes on head (2/2)
Receipts/Req2297LegacyTargetDefinesTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDuplicateTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed
Regeneration: 222/222 generated files verified by 89 passing snapshot tests on head

findings.claim: The requirement asks for all generated code to carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, and allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. But `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it is valid on classes. So projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get generated formatters and resolvers with no attribute, and the 'all generated code' criterion is not met for those targets. L7 records no preference and says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2297LegacyTargetDefinesTests.GeneratedFormattersAreExcludedFromCodeCoverageUnderLegacyTargetDefines with InlineData NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK. It drives MessagePackGenerator with those preprocessor symbols and asserts each generated *Formatter type and the resolver carry the attribute. It fails on head because the #if guard strips the attribute. The same guard is in EnumTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, ResolverTemplate.tt and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt.

findings.claim: A user who already wrote [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their own partial resolver declaration (for example `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver][ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] partial class MyResolver {}`, which is the obvious manual workaround for this issue) no longer compiles. The generated partial declaration now adds the same attribute. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has AllowMultiple=false, so the compiler reports CS0579 (duplicate attribute). The template does not check whether the user's declaration already carries the attribute. The same applies to user-declared `[CompositeResolver]` partial classes, via CompositeResolverTemplate.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDuplicateTests.UserResolverAlreadyExcludedFromCoverage_StillCompiles. It passes on base and fails on head with CS0579 in the generated MyNs.MyResolver.g.cs.

hunches.claim: The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard drops the attribute on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it allows AttributeTargets.Class on those targets (only the Assembly target was added later). The guard is therefore unnecessary, and generated code on those targets is still counted in coverage, against 'all generated code is decorated'. Ledger L7 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Drive CSharpGeneratorDriver over a [MessagePackObject] type with CSharpParseOptions preprocessorSymbols {"NETSTANDARD2_0"}, compile the result against netstandard2.0 references, and assert that the generated formatter type symbol has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. It fails on head because the attribute is preprocessed away even though it compiles on netstandard2.0.

hunches.claim: Every generated type now embeds `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` preprocessor lines. In user projects that target netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, or multi-target with them, the generated types get no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The ledger entry L7 says to follow the requirement, which says all generated code. So the acceptance criterion is only partly met on those targets. The same code also changes for all users on modern TFMs with no opt-out, which is the intended purpose, so that part is not breaking.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile generator output in a project targeting netstandard2.0 and check via reflection or Roslyn that the generated formatter or resolver lacks ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Compare with net8.0, where it is present.

hunches.claim: The `TransformUtilities` change from `{` to `{\r\n` when the nesting type has constraints alters the generated text for every nested or generic-constrained type. Users who check in or snapshot generated output will see whitespace diffs, though behaviour is unchanged. This is an unrelated tweak to the requirement and could be a byte-level surprise for snapshot-based users.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests for nested generic types with constraints and inspect the diff on the `{` line after the constraints.

hunches.claim: The generated code uses `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` on types in `global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis`. On a TFM that is not NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK, such as netstandard2.1, netcoreapp2.x, or an old Unity profile, the attribute may be missing or lack the needed AttributeTargets. That could cause a compile error (CS0234) in user builds. The condition tests the target framework, not whether the attribute exists. Netstandard2.1 has the attribute, but other TFMs might not.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the generated output in a project for each supported TFM, including netstandard2.1, and confirm there are no CS0234 or CS0246 errors.

hunches.claim: The test asserts only that the attribute string appears somewhere in each generated file, not that it decorates the emitted type. Deleting the attribute from one of several emitted types in a file (for example FormatterCache<T> or GetFormatterHelper in the resolver) would not fail it, because the resolver file still contains other occurrences.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs:64 delete-statement: remove the guarded [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] before GetFormatterHelper -> no attribute; expected to survive because AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage uses text.Contains per file and the guard test only requires attributeCount > 0 with every occurrence guarded. Only the snapshot tests would catch it.

hunches.claim: The TransformUtilities change from "{" to "{\r\n" for nesting types with constraints is a behavior change with no dedicated test. The new tests use only non-nested, non-generic types, so negating or reverting the line would not fail them. Only snapshots could catch it, and only if a snapshot covers a nested generic type with constraints.

The guard test only accepts "#if
	[attr]
#endif
" or the unindented form. It never compiles the generated output with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined, and never compiles against a target framework where the attribute is absent. The guard symbols are therefore unverified as actually preventing a compile error. A wrong symbol such as a typo would still pass as long as the Guard constant in the test is the same typo.

receipt_plan.detail: All Transforms/*.cs and *.tt guards: #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK -> #if !NETSTANDARD2_1 && !NETFRAMEWORK; expected to survive in the guard test only if the Guard constant is updated alongside. Compilation under a netstandard2.0 reference set would catch it.

hunches.claim: The test TypesThatSuppressSourceGenerationGetNoGeneratedFormatter does not exercise the change. Suppression behavior is unrelated to the attribute and would pass on base, so it does not reproduce the bug.

receipt_plan.detail: Run TypesThatSuppressSourceGenerationGetNoGeneratedFormatter against the base-built generator; it is expected to pass, showing it does not detect the missing attribute.

hunches.claim: The test checks only the minimum count (generated.Count >= 5) and never asserts that specific formatter kinds were produced, such as the enum, union, or string-key formatter. If one template stopped emitting, or one kind were skipped, the loop would still pass. A template whose attribute is removed is caught only if its file is among those generated, so a missing generated file hides the gap.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/UnionTemplate.cs:30 delete-statement: remove the guarded attribute from the union formatter; expected to be caught only if the union formatter is generated. Hence assert specific file names. The count assertion >= 5 would survive a missing kind.

hunches.claim: The README says the attribute is 'only emitted for targets where it is available (not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework)'. That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. The docs present a gap in the change as if it were a platform limitation.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] class C {}` against ReferenceAssemblies.NetStandard.NetStandard20 and ReferenceAssemblies.NetFramework.Net472.Default. It compiles without errors, which contradicts README.md:1640.

hunches.claim: The README says all generated formatters and resolvers are decorated. The change does not decorate the generated GetFormatterHelper or nested helper types consistently across every template. The README also gives no way to opt out and describes no guard behaviour for custom defines, and the change adds no entry to the docs for users who want coverage of generated code.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the README wording 'All generated formatters and resolvers' with the templates under Transforms/ and check that every emitted type has the attribute. The test only checks that each generated file contains at least one attribute, not that every type has one.

residual_risk: This change touches 237 files (222 generated) in codegen-templates, tests; the highest routed risk is 7/10. 13 file(s) were routed for deep review, 2 for light review and 222 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 170 of 170 passed, 0 failed. 11 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. 5 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes); A/B review branches. By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always on, no setting. Every formatter template (FormatterTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate, EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate) and both resolver templates (ResolverTemplate, CompositeResolverTemplate, including the nested FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper classes) write `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` with no option to turn it off. The README documents this.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: The same decoration with an opt-out setting, which the requirement explicitly calls acceptable. Add a boolean option that defaults to true, for example `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` on GeneratorOptions or on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute. Pass it into each template's Info or options, wrap each `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` write in `if (options.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage)`, and document the switch in the README.
